sources.title: Human History Map research coverage ledger
sources.note: Nine exact consecutive intervals, state kind, nine border files, imported summary, missing card and unreviewed identity, chronology and borders.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Current Wikipedia-derived text describes the modern island and province rather than the medieval atlas layer.

sources.title: Human History Map 600 borders
sources.note: The exact id is absent before its first audited interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 borders
sources.note: Exact 26-position island Polygon; tested interior, western and southern Hainan points belong to the target while Xuwen and Beihai belong to Tang.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 borders
sources.note: Preserves the same target geometry and mainland Tang seam through the 900 to 1000 interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 borders
sources.note: Retains the island Polygon with tiny coordinate quantization drift; mainland tested points now belong to Song.

sources.title: Human History Map 1100 borders
sources.note: Returns to the initial component hash while the mainland seam remains Song.

sources.title: Human History Map 1200 borders
sources.note: Exact target coverage through the last Song-era century of the atlas layer.

sources.title: Human History Map 1279 borders
sources.note: Target persists while Xuwen and Beihai switch to Yuan; the island geometry changes only by minute coordinate drift.

sources.title: Human History Map 1300 borders
sources.note: Preserves the 1279 target component and Yuan mainland seam.

sources.title: Human History Map 1400 borders
sources.note: Target still covers the island while audited mainland points are claimed by overlapping Yuan and Ming layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 1492 borders
sources.note: The target disappears; audited island points have no automatic owner while the mainland belongs to Ming.

sources.title: Hainan Museum: an introduction to Hainan history
sources.note: Provincial museum chronology covers Tang roads and migration, Song maritime traffic, Yuan administration and Ming Qiongzhou Prefecture.

sources.title: Hainan Museum: Hainan minority cultures exhibition
sources.note: Museum overview presents houses, textiles, hair ornaments, music, games and tools; used as later material-culture comparison, not automatic medieval fact.

sources.title: Tang governance and social change on Hainan
sources.note: Hainan University article analyzes Tang county building, Feng-Xian family mediation, loose administration and local resistance.

sources.title: Yuan governance of Hainan
sources.note: Hainan University article examines household registration, taxation, corvée, divided jurisdiction and incomplete control.

sources.title: Song educational expansion and cultural order on Hainan
sources.note: Scholarly article analyzes schools, examinations, ritual institutions and uneven regional reach during Song rule.

sources.title: Central Hainan in the Song and Yuan periods
sources.note: Research report discusses special institutions, agriculture, incense, migration, contact and differences between interior and coast.

sources.title: Research on Li resistance in Ming Hainan
sources.note: Hainan University journal article studies causes and patterns of Ming-period armed resistance and state suppression.

sources.title: Government officials and frontier development in Ming Hainan
sources.note: Academic study links officials with farming, schools and registration while documenting the state-building perspective and its limits.

sources.title: Landscape and garden history of Hainan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed landscape-history synthesis identifies Tang to Ming elite sites while warning that later rebuilding complicates medieval reconstruction.

sources.title: Hainan Tropical Rainforest and the traditional settlement of the Li ethnic group
sources.note: UNESCO tentative-list record explains mountain rainforest ecology and long settlement continuity; modern ethnic framing is not projected unchanged backward.

sources.title: Hainan climate and geography
sources.note: Provincial government overview describes tropical monsoon patterns, east-west rainfall differences and typhoon, drought and cold risks.

sources.title: Human impacts recorded in sediments off eastern Hainan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed multiproxy core study associates larger Sui to Tang and Song migration with changing erosion and vegetation while stating chronological limitations.

sources.title: Late Quaternary environment at Shuangchi Maar
sources.note: Radiocarbon, pollen and charcoal research reconstructs environmental change and demonstrates what lake sediments can and cannot resolve.

sources.title: Major rivers of Hainan
sources.note: Provincial overview traces major rivers from the central mountains and helps explain settlement, irrigation and transport opportunities.

sources.title: From Li people to Li ethnicity
sources.note: Chinese University of Hong Kong research explains how missionaries, ethnographers and states helped construct the modern Li ethnic category.

sources.title: Genomic history of Hlai-speaking populations
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed genomic study models complex ancestry and relationships among sampled modern groups; it is not a map of medieval identity.

sources.title: Genetic study of southern Chinese ancestry
sources.note: Chinese Academy of Sciences summary reports population-genetic results and cautions through method that ancestry is not equivalent to dynasty or ethnic label.

sources.title: Language vitality among Hlai communities
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study distinguishes Hlai varieties and notes that the current Latin-based writing system was created in 1957.

sources.title: Mitochondrial diversity of Hainan populations
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study explores deep population histories; molecular estimates carry uncertainty and cannot name medieval communities individually.

sources.title: Traditional Li textile techniques
sources.note: UNESCO documents living spinning, dyeing, weaving and embroidery skills, women’s work and mother-to-daughter teaching; used as later continuity comparison.

sources.title: Boat-shaped houses and ecological adaptation on Hainan
sources.note: Recent open study analyzes surviving villages and environmental adaptation; present structures are comparison evidence, not securely dated medieval houses.

sources.title: Hainan transit trade during the Song
sources.note: Hainan University article examines the island’s role in routes and exchange rather than imagining every resident as an overseas merchant.

sources.title: Maritime trade around Hainan in the Tang
sources.note: Scholarly chapter assembles sparse texts and archaeological evidence for routes and trade, while acknowledging documentary gaps.

sources.title: Song maritime trade patterns from shipwreck cargoes
sources.note: Peer-reviewed cargo analysis distinguishes official and small-scale networks; used as regional context rather than proof for every Hainan port.

sources.title: Hainan Museum: archaeology of the Maritime Silk Road
sources.note: Museum research discusses Jianzhen, recorded spices and offshore discoveries, with location limits kept explicit.

sources.title: Coins from the North Reef shipwreck landscape
sources.note: Scientific heritage study dates Tang through early Ming coins from offshore contexts; finds show routes, not island-wide ownership.

sources.title: Huang Daopo and Hainan textile technology
sources.note: Hainan University article assesses traditions connecting the late Song craftswoman with Li cotton tools and techniques.

sources.title: Cotton and textile exchange in Song to Yuan sources
sources.note: Xiamen University research uses primary texts on Hainan cotton goods and stresses a cross-cultural, multi-stage technology history.

sources.title: Historical irrigation and food plants on Hainan
sources.note: Provincial newspaper synthesis cites local gazetteers for Song waterworks, yam references and a 1489 Hongzhi-period canal.

sources.title: Yazhou Ancient City
sources.note: Official Sanya destination record outlines Song and Ming town development; surviving walls and street form include later rebuilding.

sources.title: Historical use of areca in Hainan medicine
sources.note: Hainan Medical University historical study follows changing knowledge of betel nut from early texts through Song medicine.

sources.title: History of Chinese medicine in Hainan
sources.note: Indexed history article reports Song-era growth and later Ming medical offices while revealing the institutional focus of surviving sources.

sources.title: Su Shi’s health practices during Hainan exile
sources.note: Medical-history article examines the exiled scholar’s diet, rest and self-care; one literate elite man is not a population sample.

sources.title: Medicine under the Song state
sources.note: Chinese Academy of Sciences book page summarizes wider Song medical institutions, used only as mainland context for uneven island access.

sources.title: Su Shi and the poem written on crossing the sea in 1100
sources.note: University cultural-history page gives the date, title and exact Classical Chinese text of June 1100.

sources.title: Su Shi in Danzhou, Hainan
sources.note: Provincial government feature localizes Su Shi’s 1097 to 1100 exile and activities in Danzhou.

sources.title: National Palace Museum spotlight on Su Shi
sources.note: Museum exhibition page independently notes his return from Danzhou and preserves the broader calligraphic context of elite writing.

sources.title: Penal exile in Tang China
sources.note: Academia Sinica research examines journeys, hard labor, unfreedom and reintegration rather than romanticizing southern exile.

sources.title: Exiled officials and Hainan in the Song
sources.note: University thesis studies hardship, cultural interaction and the source bias created by famous banished officials.

sources.title: Jianzhen’s landing in Yazhou
sources.note: Yazhou government history recounts the monk’s 748 landing and stay; later commemoration is distinguished from contemporary evidence.

sources.title: Yazhou folk-song tradition
sources.note: China intangible-heritage record documents oral transmission and claimed older influences; present tradition is not treated as a securely recorded medieval performance.

sources.title: Collective hunting in Li historical records
sources.note: Hainan University study discusses later written descriptions of organized hunting and their limits for earlier centuries.

sources.title: Hainan Museum archaeological research overview
sources.note: Provincial museum account explains field survey, excavations and offshore work while locating finds beyond the atlas polygon when necessary.

proposedOverrides.summary: An evidence-aware guide to Hainan’s changing dynastic administration, diverse island communities, environment, exile, farming, textiles, trade, learning, medicine and sanitation from 700 to the atlas layer’s editorial end in 1492.
